newsitem.title: USA: FBI probing Cooper Hospital, N.J., bonds -- paper.
newsitem.headline: FBI probing Cooper Hospital, N.J., bonds -- paper.

text.p: The FBI is investigating whether Cooper Hospital-University Medical Center in Camden, N.J., violated federal disclosure laws on a $69.4 million February bond sale, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Thursday.

The newspaper, citing unnamed federal officials, said the probe centers on whether Cooper inadequately disclosed hospital financial problems in its bond prospectus, including how millions of dollars had been lost to fraud.
Hospital officials were not immediately available for comment on the report Thursday.

In an interview with the newspaper, Cooper's board chairman, Peter Driscoll, said he could not comment on an unreleased audit that reportedly details the fraud. But he said the hospital believes at least $13 million was fraudulently taken from 1988 to 1995.
Gov. Christine Whitman said the state might consider withholding Medicaid payments to Cooper if the hospital continued refusing to release the audit.
Cooper officials told the newspaper they are convinced the bonds met the Securities and Exchange Commission's standards for disclosure.

The bonds were sold through the Camden County Improvement Authority and underwritten by Lehman Brothers, a unit of Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. Lehman officials were not immediately available for comment.
A spokeswoman for the FBI in Philadelphia, Linda Vizi, said the bureau cannot confirm or deny investigations.
